thread:
Anya: Heads-up — onboarding neoFlux-14B (int4) today. Canary started but seeing coldstart OOMs on warmup bursts and memory fragmentation causing latency spikes. Sharing quick logs and config.
Mohit: Can you paste the /var/log/runtime snippet? curious if it's prefault or KV cache related :eyes:
Anya: sure — main failure excerpt:
```
E 03:12:01 oom: alloc failed for tensor workspace (requested 427MB), available 120MB
W 03:12:01 slab: fragmented: free_chunks=12 largest=48MB
I 03:12:02 evict: triggered kv-trim (evicted 3 entries)
```
Mohit: looks like fragmentation + big allocation during max_new_tokens blowout. What are the defaults you rolled?
Anya: defaults we pushed for the canary:
```
model: neoFlux-14B-int4
max_new_tokens: 512
batch_size: 8
prefetch_kv: true
reserve_memory_mb: 0
```
Jake: 512 + batch 8 is aggressive for int4 14B on our current slot. Recommend dropping max_new_tokens to 256 and batch_size to 4 for canary ramp.
Sarah: agree. Also try turning off prefetch_kv for the first 10% canary so we don't pre-allocate large KV windows. Prefetch helps later but kills coldstart.
Eli: fragmentation hint — our slab allocator holds many small freed segments during rollout. Two mitigations: a) increase reserve_memory_mb to 180-220MB (quick), b) bump slab_reclaim_interval to 5s so we compact more aggressively. I'd try reserve first.
Anya: updated config proposal:
```
{
  "model": "neoFlux-14B-int4",
  "defaults": {
    "max_new_tokens": 256,
    "batch_size": 4,
    "prefetch_kv": false,
    "reserve_memory_mb": 200,
    "slab_reclaim_interval_sec": 5
  }
}
```
runtime-bot: canary-rollout started: neoFlux-14B-int4 @ 5% with new defaults (initiated by Anya)
Mohit: good. Also add a soft-fallback policy: if OOM rate > 1% over 5m, route to neoFlux-13B-compat automatically. That saves customers and reduces alert noise.
Anya: added fallback in rollout policy. Will run eval harness (latency+quality) after a 30m soak. Early microbench with these defaults: p95 latency dropped ~18%, mem headroom +210MB, quality delta: BLEU-like metric ~ -0.2% (within tolerance).
Jake: small quality dip expected with lower max_new_tokens but likely fine for most routes. For long-form customers we can pin to 14B with dedicated slots.
deploy-bot: canary @5% -> 10% (monitoring) :thumbsup:
Sarah: action items: 1) update default config in model-catalog (Anya), 2) add fallback route (Mohit), 3) monitor p95/p99, oom_count, kv-evictions (Jake/Eli). If oom persists, escalate to slot increase or fallback to 13B.
Anya: thanks — I'll push the catalog change and post a short runbook in #eng-ml if we need to roll back. Will post results after 30m soak :party_parrot:
Eli: FYI I'll open a quick patch to reduce allocator fragmentation risk in next minor runtime release (low-risk).
Anya: closing loop: initial 2-hour canary showed zero OOMs with new defaults and fallback triggered zero times. Moving canary to 25% and keeping monitors on. Will follow up with perf numbers and customer-facing notes.
